claim_scope: A unit mean-difference direction fit only on layer-3 residual activations from 24 regular Pythia-70m training prompts predicts grammatical number on 24 unseen regular, irregular, and nonce prompts, but 548 of all 4,096 pair-preserving label-swap nulls also reach accuracy 1.0 (p=0.134, p95=1.0), so decoding alone is not significant. A final-token-ID lookup is at chance. Replacing the direction component through a real block-3 hook changes downstream are-versus-is logits in both directions by 8.48 and 9.62, versus separate 64-direction coefficient-matched orthogonal p95 values 1.09 and 1.85. The suffix rule remains perfect on regular and nonce rows and fails only on irregulars. Embedding and orthographic baselines expose lexical structure. Each causal direction must also beat 256 fixed-seed decoder directions fit from within-pair training-label swaps with the same per-example edit sizes; both Monte Carlo plus-one p-values must be below 0.05. This is causal sensitivity in a controlled prompt family, not a unique feature, complete agreement circuit, or general verbalization benchmark.

gpu_test.claim: Pythia-70m's embedding already linearly separates this prompt family, so held-out decoding is a lexical negative result. A train-only direction still has bidirectional causal effects that exceed precommitted within-pair decoder nulls, while an operationalized explanation loop revises an s-suffix story using validation counterexamples.
